title: Dependability Field Lab — Launch proposal & test plan
content:
Purpose:

This doc proposes a short, controlled field lab to validate cross-functional SLO operational runways and fallback behaviour for model-serving workloads. Goal is to run a 6-week experiment that simulates production-like pressure across Hosted API and Dedicated paths, validate our SLO telemetry, and exercise automated fallback policies without impacting customer-facing SLAs.

Background / Why now:
- Multiple teams (Serving runtime, Platform, SRE, Product-hosted-api) have interdependent migrations (autoscaler tweaks, KV-cache changes, routing policy updates) scheduled over Q2. We need a low-risk environment to validate SLO observability and interlock procedures before full rollout.
- Current gaps: SLO signal discrepancies between token-level traces and per-route dashboards, unclear on-call responsibilities when model-variant fallbacks trigger, and untested canary rollback automation when latency or error budget burn exceeds thresholds.

Hypothesis:
1) With a coordinated field lab we can detect and repair cross-system SLO signal misalignments (tracing vs. aggregated metrics) within 72 hours.
2) Automated fallback policies can reduce customer-visible error rate by 60% during capacity degradation while keeping p50/p95 latency within 1.5x baseline.

Scope (in):
- Hosted API + Dedicated test clusters (non-prod instances pinned to sandbox credentials).
- Synthetic traffic generator that mirrors customer request size distribution (including long-context prompts).
- Telemetry feeds: token-level traces, per-route latency histograms, error budgets, cache hit/miss rates.
- Exercise model fallback, region failover, and autoscaler stress scenarios.

Non-goals (out of scope):
- Private (VPC) on-prem deployments in this run.
- Long-term billing/chargeback analysis (post-field-lab follow-up).

Success metrics (what counts as success):
- SLO signal parity: independent trace-driven SLA vs. aggregated SLO measure <5% difference for p95 latency and availability over 24h windows.
- Fallback efficacy: when fallback invoked under simulated capacity loss, customer-visible error rate reduces by >=50% within 5 minutes.
- Ops run-rate: cross-team incident response time to triage and implement rollback <= 60 minutes for simulated degradation scenarios.
- Runbook validation: all runbook steps executed once, and any ambiguous steps clarified and captured.

Experiment design / test matrix:
- Week 0 (prep): install synthetic workload generator, confirm sandbox credentials, set up dashboards and alerting channels.
- Week 1-2 (smoke): light load, verify telemetry, verify canary routing works, perform dry-run of fallback.
- Week 3-4 (pressure): ramp to 80% of observed peak; introduce KV-cache thrash, a slow kernel on a subset of GPUs, and region latency spikes.
- Week 5 (failure scenarios): simulate pod eviction and model corruption for a model-variant; observe fallback and rollback automation.
- Week 6 (retrospective): capture findings, fix high-priority action items, plan roll-forward to prod.

Canary & traffic plan:
- Canary group A: 2% of synthetic traffic routed to runbook-enabled variant. Monitor for 24h.
- Canary group B: 10% traffic after group A green.
- Progressive ramp with gating rules: stop if error budget burn >10% in 15m window or p95 latency >2x baseline for 10m.

Roles & responsibilities (cross-functional):
- SRE (Lead): Marcus Lee — test harness, alerting thresholds, runbook steward.
- Serving Runtime: Samantha Chen — kernel selection, KV-cache instrumentation, fallback triggers.
- Platform / Infra: Diego Alvarez — sandbox cluster config, autoscaler policies, capacity simulation.
- Product / Hosted API: Aisha Patel (owner) — endpoint routing policies, customer impact assessment, public comms templates.
- Observability: Triage buddy rotation (list to be attached) — validate signals, reconcile anomalies.

Key runbook excerpts to validate:
- Fallback activation checklist: detection > validate > route > notify > monitor > escalate.
- Rollback automation: conditions to auto-roll back to earlier model variant (and circuit-breaker thresholds).
- Communication play: slack #service-ops, incident bridge template, customer status page update template.

Instrumentation & dashboards to create:
- Token-level latency ribbon aligned with per-route aggregated p50/p95/p99.
- Error budget burn-rate heatmap with 1m/5m windows and sources (model, infra, network).
- Cache-miss cascade chart tied to CPU/GPU utilization.

Dependencies & linked work:
- JIRA SRE-9876: field lab infra provisioning (must complete week 0).
- GitHub PR #42: synthetic workload generator improvements (needs merge before Week 1).
- Confluence DEP-FIELDLAB-2026: detailed test scripts and synthetic profile definitions.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Synthetic load accidentally leaks into prod routing. Mitigation: sandbox network ACLs, separate API keys, IP allowlist.
- Risk: Alert fatigue from noisy thresholds. Mitigation: use temporary experiment-only alert routing to an ops queue and throttle non-critical notifications.
- Risk: Cross-team scheduling conflicts. Mitigation: block recurring 2-hour windows for core teams during Weeks 2-5.

Rollback & safety knobs:
- Global kill-switch: platform API to stop the synthetic generator and pause canaries (documented command).
- Immediate fallback: switch to pre-warmed model-variant and disable batching for affected route.

Communication plan:
- Pre-launch: short pre-brief in Weekly SRE sync and Slack announcement with schedule and contact list.
- During run: dedicated #dependability-fieldlab channel; page for exec updates if customer impact > medium.
- Post-run: 45-minute retrospective with action owner assignments and timeline for fixes.

Artifacts to produce by end of lab:
- Updated runbook with precise commands and verification steps.
- Incident playbook mapping: SRE -> Serving -> Platform handover matrix.
- Dashboard pack and sample alert templates for production rollout.

Next steps (immediate):
1) Confirm participants and reserve sandbox clusters (Owner: Diego, due 2026-03-05).
2) Merge synthetic workload PR and stage generator in sandbox (Owner: Marcus, due 2026-03-08).
3) Create experiment dashboards + alert routing (Owner: Observability lead, due 2026-03-10).

Notes to self / loose items:
- Verify token-trace retention window covers full pressure test (possible retention extension).
- Check whether model-variant metadata is propagated to logs for easier triage.
- Add a small UX test: ensure 503->fallback path preserves user context in token streams.

Meeting log (prep call 2026-02-26):
- Agreed on 6-week cadence; prioritized telemetry parity and fallback rollbacks.
- Action: Marcus to draft gating rules; Samantha to add KV-cache counters; Diego to provision two non-prod clusters.

If this looks good I will convert to a small Jira epic and invite the cross-functional kick-off.

-- Aisha P.
